claims.claim_text: The indexed Edgar N. Brooks is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and the official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier and exact normalized full name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated July 17, 1943; the index documents an OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: Obituary, cemetery, military, and directory namesakes lacking the identifier or Box 82 linkage were rejected.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry, Edgar N. Brooks was recorded in a residual miscellaneous-products manufacturing occupation group.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official record carries code 513; NARA's official numerical list maps 5-13 to a miscellaneous-products manufacturing group.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private identifier and exact full indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on July 17, 1943; its relation to OSS recruitment remains unknown.
claims.match_notes: No exact trade, product, employer, plant, workplace, or immediate OSS predecessor is inferred from the residual code.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Ernest Brooks, Jr. is a high-confidence match to the Ernest Brooks, Jr. whose family sought CIA information about his London OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: World War II service in London as a member of the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1986 letter from the Director of Central Intelligence expressly identifies Ernest Brooks, Jr. as an OSS member who served in London.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact name and suffix plus an official, person-specific OSS service reference; no private identifier appears in the CIA letter.
claims.temporal_assessment: The CIA letter establishes wartime OSS service in London but gives no recruitment or separation dates.
claims.match_notes: The uncommon suffix-bearing OSS match is substantially stronger than name-only results, but Box 82 should still be reviewed for a direct personnel-file crosswalk.

claims.claim_text: Ernest Brooks, Jr. is documented as counsel with Breed, Abbott & Morgan in 1937 and 1938, before his wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Breed, Abbott & Morgan ... Ernest Brooks, Jr.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two contemporary reported decisions list Ernest Brooks, Jr. among counsel associated with Breed, Abbott & Morgan.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Medium-confidence career linkage: exact name and suffix, two contemporary firm records, official CIA OSS identity, and a corroborative biographical bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented in 1937 and 1938, before the independently documented wartime OSS service; immediacy is not established.
claims.match_notes: The firm is not labeled the immediate pre-OSS employer or last civilian employer. Box 82 is needed to confirm the career crosswalk and recruitment chronology.
